content.thinking:
I'm drafting the paragraph now. The slowdown hit account pages, and since the cause ties the extra work to how many purchases a shopper has made, the people with longer histories were hit hardest. I'm wondering whether "many things" implies a number I don't have, so I'll avoid it and say the pages loaded slowly for some shoppers, worst for those with longer purchase histories, matching the cause.

Nobody was paged, so the response cost fell on no one. Argus estimated the customer loss as a figure I haven't seen yet. Argus rolled the deployment back, the rollback is confirmed and still in place, and automatic sync stays off. The proposed fix, PR #565, is a draft and hasn't been applied.

input.overview: For {duration}, account pages on the io-shop website loaded slowly. A code change to how the shop works out a shopper's average spend made it add up that shopper's purchases again and again instead of once. The more items a shopper had bought, the more work this created, so shoppers with more purchases saw the biggest slowdown. Argus estimates the cost to the shop in lost sales at {customer_loss}. Nobody was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one, so the response took no on-call staff time. Argus rolled back the io-shop deployment that introduced the change. The rollback is confirmed and still in place, and automatic sync has been left off. Argus has also proposed a permanent fix, PR #565, but it is still a draft and has not been applied.
